118	### Step wiring
119	
120	Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
121	point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
122	method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
123	`method:`.
124	
125	- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
126	  as `@Parameter T`.
127	- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
128	  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
129	  branch; not calling it short-circuits.
130	
131	### Function parameters
132	
133	Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:
134	
135	- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
136	- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
137	- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
138	  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
139	  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
140	- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
141	  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

145	Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
146	into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):
147	
148	- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
149	- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a

# OfficeFloor REST wiring

Domain REST endpoints are declared here as OfficeFloor YAML, served by the
`officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` inside the Spring Boot host. Put them under `rest/api/` so
their paths start with `/api/` — `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend; a non-`/api/`
path returns the SPA's `index.html` instead of your endpoint. Directory nesting maps to path
segments, so `rest/api/owners.GET.yml` → `GET /api/owners`. Each route is its own file:

```
# officefloor/rest/api/<path>.GET.yml   (or .POST.yml, {param}.GET.yml, ...)
service:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.<SomeLogic>   # a class with a service(...) method
```

The logic class's `service(...)` method takes injected dependencies (Spring `@Service` beans, the
data layer) and a `net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse<T>` to send the response.

(The `/actuator/health` readiness endpoint is Spring-side — Actuator — not an OfficeFloor route.)

# OfficeFloor REST wiring

Domain REST endpoints are declared here as OfficeFloor YAML, served by the
`officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` inside the Spring Boot host. Put them under `rest/api/` so
their paths start with `/api/` — `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend; a non-`/api/`
path returns the SPA's `index.html` instead of your endpoint. Directory nesting maps to path
segments, so `rest/api/owners.GET.yml` → `GET /api/owners`. Each route is its own file:

```
# officefloor/rest/api/<path>.GET.yml   (or .POST.yml, {param}.GET.yml, ...)
service:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.<SomeLogic>   # a class with a service(...) method
```

The logic class's `service(...)` method takes injected dependencies (Spring `@Service` beans, the
data layer) and a `net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse<T>` to send the response.

(The `/actuator/health` readiness endpoint is Spring-side — Actuator — not an OfficeFloor route.)

Stewards can now re-date an OPEN or PENDING claim, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it behaves**
- **Who and which claims:** only a steward can re-date, and only an OPEN or PENDING claim. Anyone else, or a claim in any other state, gets an error on the claim.
- **Other refusals:** a new date after the person's retirement is refused. So is a claim whose current date is in a closed period, or a new date that falls inside one. A refused re-date changes nothing in the store and writes nothing to the audit file.
- **What stays the same:** the due-by keeps the date it was given when the claim was added. A figure bound by a statement stays bound.
- **What follows the new date:** the claim's period. If per-period numbering is on and the new date lands in a different period, the claim gets the next number in that period's sequence. The old number is never reused, because each period's count only goes up.
- **Audit:** a successful re-date writes `CLAIM_REDATED … number=<n> old=<old date> new=<new date>`. If any figures moved, the usual ROLLUP/TOTALS lines follow.

**What I changed**
- **Endpoint:** `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/redate?date=…`, in `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/redate.POST.yml`. It follows the same pattern as the existing reassign endpoint.
- **Server classes:** `RedateClaim`, `SaveRedating`, `RecordClaimRedated` and `Redating`, plus a `ClaimRepository.redate` method that saves the date and number. No database migration was needed.
- **Front end:** in `PersonClaims.tsx`, each claim now has a date box (`claim-date-new`) and a "Re-date" button (`claim-redate`), with the error shown in `claim-error`. Taking any other action on the claim, or changing the date, clears an old re-date error. The call itself is `redateClaim` in `features/claims/api.ts`.

Two choices of mine you may want to change:
- The steward check is fixed in code rather than added as a new entry in the sheet's permission settings, because the request says "anyone but a steward". This works like approve and reject.
- A claim that keeps its period keeps its number, even when numbering is on.
